result:
**Round 25 verdict: PASS.** A's Master Volume, Master Mute and export overload warning all hold up when used in the real Studio. Every check below is from my own runs; I didn't take A's numbers on trust. One existing bug, C-R23-01, got worse this round.

**Live playback** (real key presses and clicks in the browser, measuring the actual audio output):
- **Master Volume:** setting ΓêÆ6 dB lowered the mix by exactly 6.000 dB in all 3 runs, and going back to 0 dB restored it exactly. The playhead kept running, no new audio graph was built, and new sounds only started at normal loop boundaries.
- **Master Mute:** the output fell below ΓêÆ60 dBFS within 14 ms of the click and was fully silent from 60 ms on. Unmuting came back to the same level with no overshoot. The fade-out drops steadily with no click in 3 valid runs (one run was thrown out for a recording glitch and replaced).
- **Video sound:** Master Mute silences the video's own sound too. The video stayed within 20 ms of the audio and never paused.
- **Undo/Redo:** after Master Mute, Undo brings the sound back and Redo silences it again, live during playback. The loop seam is unchanged: 0 ms gap, quietest 5 ms at a wrap ΓêÆ24.5 dBFS.

**Export** (real dialog clicks, then decoding the WAV files):
- **0 dB:** 18.000 s, 1800 full-scale samples, RMS ΓêÆ15.48. These match round 24.
- **Overload alert:** the text matches the spec exactly: "+5.0 dBFS ΓÇö 1800 sample ΓÇö reduce Master by 5.0 dB". I worked out the peak independently from the ΓêÆ6 dB file and got +4.995, which rounds to +5.0. Exporting again at ΓêÆ5.0 dB gives 0 full-scale samples and no alert.
- **ΓêÆ6 dB:** the samples are scaled by exactly 0.501187.
- **Muted:** the warning note shows before export, the button stays enabled, and the file is a real 18 s of silence.

**History, keyboard and layout:**
- 12 arrow presses make 12 history entries on the Master fader, the same as on a track Volume. A mouse drag makes one entry.
- Tab goes ΓåÉ CZABA ΓåÆ Master Mute ΓåÆ Master Volume ΓåÆ Play. Home on the fader sets ΓêÆ60 dB and doesn't move the playhead.
- Header, transport, lane rows and the floating video are pixel-identical to round 24 at both 1280├ù720 and 1440├ù900. No Master text is clipped.

**Gates:**
- Type check: 0 errors. Tests: 1045/1045. Build passes. Biome: 0 errors.
- All four of my code mutations were caught by A's tests.
- Git status is exactly the expected 54 lines, and nothing outside A's allowed files changed.
- Premium access is not bypassed. A fresh logged-out session opens the demo and can export. `/studio/middle-east` asks to sign in, and the token endpoint returns 401.

**Worse this round: C-R23-01** (medium, already open). The server-rendered `/studio-lab` HTML now has 8 corrupted bytes instead of 4. Three of them hit visible Georgian text before the page finishes loading: the demo badge, a library line and the "Arrangement ┬╖" heading. After load the text corrects itself, and the Master labels are clean. The Master code itself is fine; the new header markup just shifted where the corruption lands. It still needs the Tech Lead's choice between React 19 and a narrow `entry.server.tsx` change, and that is now more urgent.

**Notes for B (not bugs):**
- Two exports of the same project differ by 1 step at 24-bit (inaudible); this was already seen in round 11. So "byte-identical export" can't be used as a test oracle; use the stats or a ┬▒1-step tolerance.
- When muted with a non-zero gain, the dialog shows both "silent file" and "Master ΓêÆ5.0 dB is included", which reads as contradictory.
- The fader is only 4 px tall to grab with a mouse, the same as the track faders.
- I switched how I judged the mute fade after the first three runs. The result also passes at zero tolerance, and the report says so.

The root review findings (hardcoded middle-east loader, Lenis, the uncommitted 54-line tree, the Modal focus gap and the rest) are unchanged and listed in the report for B.
